ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in $\odot O$, with $E$ being a point on the extension of $BC$, and point $C$ being the midpoint of the arc $\overset{\frown}{BD}$. If $\angle DCE=110^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in circle O,\\
it follows that $\angle DCE=\angle BAD$ \\
Since $\angle DCE=110^\circ$ \\
then $\angle BAD=110^\circ$ \\
Given that point C is the midpoint of the arc $BD$\\
it follows that arc $BC=$ arc $DC$ \\
Therefore, $\angle BAC=\angle DAC=\frac{1}{2}\angle BAD=\frac{1}{2}\times 110^\circ=55^\circ$ \\
Hence, the measure of $\angle BAC$ is $\boxed{55^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and the four points A, B, C, and D are all on the circle, forming the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD. B is on the left side, C is above, D is at the lower right, and A is at the lower left; the line segment BC is extended through C toward the upper right to point E, so CE is the extension line of BC. The figure also draws connecting lines such as AC, CD, and AD, therefore ∠DCE is the exterior angle at point C formed by CD and the extension line CE of BC. Reasoning: According to the exterior angle theorem for a cyclic quadrilateral, the exterior angle ∠DCE at point C of the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD is equal to its opposite interior angle ∠BAD. Therefore ∠BAD = ∠DCE = 110°. Also because C is the midpoint of arc BD, arc BC and arc CD are equal; inscribed angles subtended by the same arc or equal arcs are equal, therefore ∠BAC = ∠CAD. AC divides ∠BAD into two equal angles, ∠BAC and ∠CAD, so ∠BAC = 110° ÷ 2 = 55°.
